look_here_first: FIRST find the slender open starburst of four pale SEPALS (no true petals) and numerous exposed stamens; purple/scarlet leatherflowers instead hang as leathery urns. Notice opposite compound often deeply LOBED leaflets and a twisting LEAF STALK that clasps supports. Male and female flowers occur on separate vines; only female vines produce the famous shaggy long (4–9 cm) silky style/beak heads. Avoid confusing an introduced white sweet autumn clematis with smooth-edged leaflets and massive bisexual bloom sprays.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Woody scrambling/climbing vine, often several meters.

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Usually odd-pinnate and 5-foliolate; leaflets often deeply divided or cleft.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Open rather than urn-shaped; four thin white/cream spreading sepals; male and female flowers on separate vines.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Aggregate achenes with very long silky plumose beaks forming conspicuous 'old man's beard' masses.

key_traits.label: Family backfill note
key_traits.text: Ranunculaceae family backfill uses C. drummondii as the open-flower Clematis anchor: petaloid sepals + many free stamens/pistils + aggregate achenes.
